point_of_contention: Is the retired shield-damage-reduction defect confined to the single Parry row on this sheet, so that a one-site deletion settles it, or does it survive at a second site that a mirror-scoped search cannot reach, and what repair scope follows from the answer?
reasoning: The site-level argument stands: the refute position names the Parry row as a carrier of the retired shield-DR claim, shows that row contradicting its own document's defense summary, and the opposing round-2 finding concedes that this chapter-scoped wording stands as written, so the existence of the defect at this site is common ground. What is contested is scope, and there the sole-carrier claim goes undefended: one side asserts the defect lives at a single site and repairs it by deletion, while the rebuttal supplies a concrete second carrier (a bestiary Guard line that adds a point of reduction), notes that a mirror-scoped search cannot reach it, and grounds its practical effect in this sheet's own Standard encounter row that fields a Knight beside six Guards. No argument in the record answers that second site, and the classification offered to bound the carrier set at two is likewise left unanswered. On the arguments as presented, the higher-confidence single-site position is a claim about one row, not about the class, and the class stands under-counted until re-derived; the repair therefore cannot be a blanket deletion, because in a creature stat block the same wording carries protection the author priced, which must be folded into the creature's authored reduction total or removed together with the line rather than stripped blindly.
ruling: The council must treat the Parry-row shield-reduction claim as established and must not scope the repair as a single-site deletion: the clause comes out of this sheet's Parry row outright, and any site list inherited from a mirror-scoped search must be re-derived and the repair defined per site before edits are scoped.
